examples.before: big: 1234567890…(the same 10 digits repeated, several thousand digits in all)
examples.input: `config get big` (a stored integer several thousand digits long)

results.1: exit 0, nothing on stderr; prints the whole number on one line (the capture cut off the last 131 bytes); no digit-limit error
results.2: exit 0, nothing on stderr; prints the whole number on one line (the capture cut off the last 131 bytes); no digit-limit error

context.in_practice: All three implementations on each route gave identical results on every command. You can't tell the routes apart from what a user sees here. Both print YAML values in their resolved form rather than as written: `1e3` becomes `1000.0`, `0x1F` becomes `31`, `~` becomes `null` and `-.inf` becomes `-inf`. Every output ends with one newline.
context.stakes: When you read a setting with `config get` or `config show`, the value printed is what scripts and people will copy. A huge integer, a float written as `1e3`, a hex number, `-.inf` or a YAML null each need to come out in a predictable form without crashing. In these tests both routes printed exactly the same thing for every case.
context.tradeoff: Route 1 sets the printing rules on purpose: lower-case null/true/false, floats in full form, integers as plain digits. One of its implementations dropped special handling for very long integers as unneeded. Route 2 never addressed printing at all, yet its output matched route 1 on every case tested.

plan_why: Prints different kinds of scalars with get/show: an integer of 4400 digits (over Python's 4300-digit str() limit, the handling one implementation removed), a float written in exponent form, negative infinity, a hex integer and a null written as ~; this shows whether each prints Python repr/str forms with lower-case null and one trailing newline, or fails.
routes: null/true/false lower-case, floats via repr, ints via str, one trailing newline
